card.title: Interference of light — Young's double slit experiment

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two slits fed by one source interfere. Bright fringes sit at whole-number wavelengths of path difference, and the equal spacing is λ D / d. The centre is bright. A wider slit gap packs the fringes closer, and separate lamps do not keep the phase steady.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
β = λD/d
a sinθ = mλ
r_m = √(mRλ)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The small-angle form needs D much greater than d.  ·  Order m = 0 is the centre.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Young's experiment lets one wavefront illuminate two narrow slits. The two waves that leave the slits stay in step, so they interfere on a distant screen. Two separate lamps do not keep that fixed phase.  ·  Where the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths, the waves arrive in phase and the fringe is bright. Where the path difference is an odd number of half wavelengths, the fringe is dark.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: • Interference of light — Young's double slit experiment  ·  One source feeds both slits.  ·  The centre is bright.  ·  Fringes are equally spaced.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Young's double slit: fringe width β = λD/d; 1st minimum of single slit: a sinθ = mλ.  ·  Newton's rings: r_m = √(mRλ) (dark/dark convention); λ = 2(rₙ₊₁² − rₙ²)/N (interferometric use).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The central fringe is bright because the two paths are equal. The bright fringes are equally spaced. The spacing is β = λ D / d, with D the screen distance and d the slit separation, when D is much larger than d.  ·  A longer wavelength, a more distant screen, or closer slits all widen the pattern. Closing one slit removes the two-source fringes and leaves the single-slit spread.  ·  White light gives a white central fringe and coloured fringes farther out, because each colour has its own spacing. The red fringes sit farther apart than the blue ones.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A larger slit separation packs them closer.  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ young's double slit: fringe width β = λd/d; 1st minimum of single slit: a sinθ = mλ..  ·  β = λ D / d, not λ d / D.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Closer slits make wider fringes.  ·  Two lamps are not coherent.  ·  D is the screen distance and d is the slit gap.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Coherence comes from splitting one wave.  ·  Write β = λ D / d and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.  ·  Brewster: i_p = arctan(n₂/n₁), reflected ray fully polarised at that angle.  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: young's double slit: fringe width β = λd/d; 1st minimum of single slit: a sinθ = mλ.  ·  The path difference at a small angle is d sinθ, or d x / D on the screen.
